messages.text: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

paragraphs:
Look, I built you a clean full-body routine that needs zero gear and fits right into a twice-a-week rhythm. Everything here is dosed from where your baseline sits right now.

Here is how we set it up:
- **Bulgarian Split Squats (Bodyweight):** 3 sets of 8 each leg. Focus on a controlled 3-second descent. That slow eccentric control is what is going to bulletproof that right knee for stair descents on Annapurna.
- **Push-ups:** 3 sets of 8. Dosed conservatively well below your 15-rep max so we don't stress the right elbow joint.
- **Single-Leg RDLs (Bodyweight):** 3 sets of 8 each leg. Keeps the load off your lower back while sorting out side-to-side balance.
- **Plank & Bird Dogs:** Core stability work that protects your back without loading it.

I locked this routine into your system as 'Bodyweight Strength Foundation'. Run it twice this week with at least two rest or active recovery days between them. How does that flow look to you?

Take your time on the descent and let the legs do the work.

messages.text: Can you build me a full-body strength routine, no equipment, for twice a week?

paragraphs:
Look, I built you a clean full-body routine that needs zero gear and fits right into a twice-a-week rhythm. Everything here is dosed from where your baseline sits right now.

Here is how we set it up:
- **Bulgarian Split Squats (Bodyweight):** 3 sets of 8 each leg. Focus on a controlled 3-second descent. That slow eccentric control is what is going to bulletproof that right knee for stair descents on Annapurna.
- **Push-ups:** 3 sets of 8. Dosed conservatively well below your 15-rep max so we don't stress the right elbow joint.
- **Single-Leg RDLs (Bodyweight):** 3 sets of 8 each leg. Keeps the load off your lower back while sorting out side-to-side balance.
- **Plank & Bird Dogs:** Core stability work that protects your back without loading it.

I locked this routine into your system as 'Bodyweight Strength Foundation'. Run it twice this week with at least two rest or active recovery days between them. How does that flow look to you?

messages.text: For today's session, use that new routine, but skip the core phase - my lower back's a bit tired. Just for today.

paragraphs: Look, that is the right call. When the lower back is feeling tired, we do not force trunk flexion or holds on top of it. Protect the plan by being smart. I took the core phase off today's session in the app. Just focus on clean, controlled reps on the split squats, push-ups, and single-leg RDLs. Take your time on the descent and let the legs do the work.

input.message: That's it for today, wrap this up.

output.reply: Good work today. You made the smart call listening to your back, and we got the right foundation built. Rest up, stay on top of recovery tonight, and we will get after it next time.

### Warmup & Activation (7-8 mins)
